summary.prose: S6 connects the completed investigation engine to daemon and MCP clients through one daemon-owned service. Both reviewer parties and source modes share pinned scope, per-block durable progress, recovery and canonical completion; indexed mode adds only caller discovery. Adoption stays opt-in behind native-tool qualification, compatibility and quality evidence, with a rollback that preserves existing runs and design-review behavior.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a1: a daemon-owned durable investigation state machine with provider-independent accepted state. Seed each run with sc1's approved tasks/checks, artifact references and explicit commit packets, not embedded source partitions. Source-only and indexed-impact runs use identical packets, obligations, reviewer policy and completion checks; only the indexed capability in sc3 differs. Substantive judgments remain the independent agent's job; deterministic guards validate identity, evidence provenance, coverage and publication, not semantic correctness. Reuse existing LLMProvider/CliProvider read-only execution, budget admission, source freshness, ownership and canonical artifact lifecycle; introduce the investigation protocol and durable accepted-state store behind the existing code-review entrypoints. Checkpoint cadence is per reviewed commit-packet block, independently of continuation boundaries and run time limits; multiple block checkpoints may be accepted within one managed reviewer session.

ownedContracts.name: ReviewClientStatusV1
ownedContracts.purpose: Versioned start/status/resume/cancel replies for MCP and daemon clients, retaining legacy CR readability and surfacing state rather than reporting transport silence as a verdict. Sole transport owner for plan-investigation-v1 code reviews, version-routed alongside predecessor 8315a11f/S005 sc7; never replaces design-review or legacy frames.

consumedContracts.name: ImmutableReviewSubjectV1
consumedContracts.purpose: The only authority for changed scope. Exact selected commit packets identify relevant parent-relative blocks; frozen context can include other source only as context. No HEAD/working-tree diff fallback.

consumedContracts.name: EvidenceCoverageV1
consumedContracts.purpose: Run-scoped evidence and many-to-many coverage bindings. Each approved obligation, packet block/non-text change and applicable criterion has a required row; findings and unresolved work cannot disappear.

consumedContracts.name: InvestigationContinuationV1
consumedContracts.purpose: One bounded independent read-only investigation protocol for both entrypoints/modes. Provider sessions execute requests but never own scope, accepted coverage or completion. Accept incremental per-block progress and durable acknowledgments inside one managed continuation; final replies reference accepted block receipts. Domain protocol only; s6 owns external MCP registration. Legacy sibling 8315a11f/S005 sc7 remains separate.

consumedContracts.name: DurableReviewRecoveryV1
consumedContracts.purpose: Daemon-owned acceptance journal, reconstructible checkpoints and exclusive generation/lease fencing; accepted replies are idempotent, uncertain provider outcomes remain explicit. Checkpoint per reviewed block, not only after a whole provider request or at the run time limit.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewCompletionV1
consumedContracts.purpose: Validate accountable coverage and source applicability before one canonical CR publication. Required unverified work blocks successful completion; findings retain existing severity/confidence and human override policy.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewRuntimePortsV1
consumedContracts.purpose: Foundational type-level ports avoid making the investigation Story depend backwards on recovery. s4 implements durable storage, s3 uses the port, and s6 composes production adapters. Usage observations flow to existing usage contracts with a durable pending outbox when a writer is unavailable.

boundary.internal: Own production composition, equivalent MCP/daemon/controller start/status/resume/cancel adapters, status/usage presentation fields, explicit engine rollout/rollback, legacy compatibility and evaluation fixtures. No client opens stores directly; no client-specific board UI or design-review replacement. Sole new-engine MCP adapter/schema owner; reconcile 8315a11f/S005 legacy sc7 as specified in the architecture and record code-only supersession before opt-in. Verify routing partitions across both installation orders.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own subject preparation, attribution ambiguity detection, exact Git commit/blob/block navigation and frozen context binding. Define foundational runtime-port types only; do not implement task investigation, a recovery store or new accounting storage. No generic HEAD/working-tree diff may select scope.

Own required-row enumeration, evidence identity/provenance and coverage relationships/dispositions. Reuse subject inputs and runtime ports. Keep ledger validation helpers private; do not execute reviewer turns or publish CRs.

Own independent read-only task-directed continuation behavior, on-demand source navigation, optional indexed caller/impact enrichment, budget admission, bounded retry/pause and attempt usage emission through foundational ports. In-memory ports are test scaffolding while production selection remains disabled until s4/s6; no durable storage implementation or terminal approval logic. Publish and acknowledge incremental block progress within continuations, with partial cross-block assessments recorded rather than lost. Domain progress contracts only; no competing MCP phase/schema ownership. External registration belongs to s6.

Own durable implementation of foundational acceptance/usage-outbox ports, append/replay/checkpoint integrity, lease/generation fencing, uncertain attempts and compatibility/time recovery. Do not alter review criteria or introduce a usage warehouse. Its recovery implementation is composed by downstream s6 rather than consumed backwards by s3. Persist/replay block-level evidence and assessment receipts independently of final provider-call completion.

Own completion coverage/freshness/party validation, canonical CR adaptation and idempotent terminal publication receipts. Reuse existing lifecycle and severity/confidence policy. Do not let a completion request, missing evidence or a failed run masquerade as a completed verdict.

nonFunctional.performance: No eager whole-source or whole-contract repetition and no mandatory call-per-clause. Bounded read ranges and explicit evidence references prevent unbounded request growth.128K inclusive estimated admission and five-minute continuation cap; default120active-minute/24continuation limits pause with durable progress and explicit extension rather than claim success. Use deterministic/mock providers for routine tests; measure authorized live comparisons against recorded baselines before claiming savings. Block checkpoint acceptance is independent of run duration:120minutes is a pause ceiling, never a save interval. Grouping several block assessments in one session remains allowed.
nonFunctional.security: Daemon owns runtime state and DB access; cloud access remains LLMProvider/CliProvider only. Independent reviewer identity is checked at start and publication. Source reads are pinned and read-only; untrusted repository text is data, not tool/policy authority. Trusted evidence reads cannot escape the declared snapshot/approved-artifact view, graph queries bind to the registered source repo and declared dependency closure, and native adapters that cannot meet pinning/read-only capability refuse explicitly. Private runtime state uses restrictive access; metadata diagnostics contain no raw prompts/evidence.
nonFunctional.observability: Expose run/subject/engine/policy IDs, owner generation, attempt lifecycle, required/covered/unverified rows, pause/stale causes and resume compatibility. Show managed attempt count/active time, observed usage quality and unknown/pending observations distinctly from reservations and estimates. Emit status/heartbeats without replaying accepted work; transport disconnect is not a review verdict. Keep human-readable review reports only in /tmp. Surface latest accepted block/progress receipt and outstanding block IDs so clients can distinguish durable block progress from provider-session liveness.
nonFunctional.durability: Journal-committed acceptance precedes acknowledgment; snapshots/checkpoints are reconstructible and verified against immutable evidence/answer blobs. Detect torn tails and corruption, fence concurrent owners and late replies, preserve uncertain provider outcomes and idempotent completion/usage receipts. Pauses do not erase consumed execution time. Legacy runs are explicitly non-resumable; runtime data remains outside artifact JSON and excluded from changed scope. Every reviewed block is journal-committed before its durable acknowledgment and cursor advancement, even while a native session continues. Accepted block state survives an uncertain or failed enclosing attempt; only unfinished/unacknowledged work is resumed.

dataModelChanges.details: Proposed shared types in src/shared/review-investigation.ts and daemon adapters in src/daemon/review-investigation-rpc.ts. Explicit engine:'plan-investigation-v1', version:1, operation start/status/resume/cancel/read/impact/progress/reply; start includes requestId UUID, registered repo identity, root/story/BUILD IDs, sc1 explicit commit/parent/attestation selections and sourceMode. The daemon derives author/reviewer from canonical BUILD and authenticated execution context, never from client fields. start returns accepted descriptor/status and, for controller execution, one sc3 turn with scoped capability. read accepts only a bounded sc1 reference; progress accepts only sc3 ReviewBlockProgressV1 and returns its durable receipt; reply accepts only sc3 InvestigationReplyV1. Existing insrc_code_review_step and codeReview.run route explicit new-engine envelopes before invoking legacy resolution/grounding. Proposed codeReview.investigation command IPC methods are additive. Legacy start/judgements or predecessor emit_calls/answers remain on their own versioned states. No engine field plus existing state always routes to its original adapter; a new explicit engine requires negotiated capability; engine/schema/generation mismatch refuses before dispatch. Never pass a new-engine request into legacy runCodeReview or generic HEAD diff on error.

Proposed src/daemon/review-investigation-service.ts owns one service per registered repo and consumes S1-S5. One start requestId maps to runId=SHA256(canonical repo ID + requestId), with exclusive admission and exact descriptor comparison; same request/scope reuses, conflicting reuse refuses. Store an immutable 0600 descriptor under the private 0700 .insrc/review-runs/production-v1 namespace, referencing sc4 run ID and immutable manifest, approved root/story/BUILD pins, packet selections, policy/profile/compatibility digest, source mode, reviewer party, adapter version and start identity. This is an immutable discovery binding, not a second acceptance journal. Create-before-run crash is a prepared admission orphan recoverable only after exact canonical revalidation; no accepted work or started attempt is inferred. RecoveryStore remains sole owner of accepted evidence, attempts, progress, leases and terminal receipts; do not alter private sc4 events or manifest layout. Caller-controlled paths never select storage; validate run IDs and registered repo realpath. Production descriptor and bridge files are private runtime, excluded from source/index/context like existing .insrc state.

Proposed src/daemon/review-investigation-adapters.ts reads daemon's existing canonical ArtifactStore/History/LifecycleService and registry; project verified work into readApprovedWork then prepareReviewSubject/buildLedgerBasis. Use committed BUILD task/change attribution and explicit selected commit/parent packets; server-generated attestations prove full/exclusive ownership or ask for explicit approved scope evidence when mixed/ambiguous. A Story trailer alone is not block exclusivity. Do not accept client claims of approval or unregistered repos. Planned scope must not bypass a present invalid PLAN; planless scope requires an explicit approved upstream basis with criteria/change rows retained. Canonical artifact evidence reads use pinned immutable revision/history and verified exact rendered text, not mutable markdown. Source reads use sc1 pinned blobs/context; verified TESTS/BUILD results bind to the same source. Source-only has no caller tool; indexed mode resolves changed entities to selected block/path/blob and uses daemon graph findCallers within registry dependency closure with source/index identity, limited rows and stale/partial/unknown markers. Empty/partial discovery cannot prove no impact. Returned caller source is separately inspected through pinned reads; unresolved applicability produces required impact rows/unverified work or accountable findings, never silent omission. No index writes or client DB access.

dataModelChanges.entity: Qualified native and controller session bindings
dataModelChanges.details: Proposed src/agent/providers/investigation-session.ts and src/mcp/review-investigation-bridge.ts provide one scoped read/impact/progress/reply catalogue bound to process epoch, run, subject, attempt, generation, requestDigest, caller role and expiry. A daemon-created capability authenticates the binding; it cannot authorize other repos, raw filesystem/shell/git/network/MCP tools, approval, or arbitrary daemon RPC. Native CLI execution uses a private isolated configuration and only this scoped bridge, with built-in/general tools disabled or denied by an independently verified adapter capability; immutable data is returned only through sc1/sc2-backed callbacks. Qualification must inspect effective tool/config isolation, not trust provider boolean claims or read-only sandbox alone. CLI-specific argument support is implemented/verified per installed adapter version; unsupported binaries refuse before issuing a model request, never fall back to existing broad runReviewSession. OAuth remains the CLI's existing session; no credential copies, direct REST or repository-authored server instructions. Bridge can ACK several blocks before a final response inside one native session. Controller hosts receive the same authorized turn/tool schemas via MCP and fresh declared host budget; server still issues/persists attempts, validates provenance and ACKs progress. Host context estimates are declared, not measured. Capability grants no general artifact write: progress invokes only sc3/sc4 validated acceptance. Disconnect retains accepted state and the bounded active attempt; reconnect may reattach only a still-active authenticated binding. Restart/expiry/cancel revokes old capabilities; resume claims a new generation and reuses accepted work, never legacy volatile state. Cancellation aborts provider/host wait and waits for draining authority before reuse; late callbacks refuse. Effective isolation also excludes inherited user/project MCP servers, plugins/hooks and repository startup instructions as executable authority; no unrestricted repository cwd or writable artifact directory is exposed to the reviewer. Only adapter/version combinations with verified isolation can be selected; deterministic fake-CLI tests alone do not certify an installed binary.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: interface QualifiedInvestigationSessionBinding { readonly version: 1; readonly bindingId: string; readonly adapterVersion: string; readonly profileDigest: string; readonly catalogDigest: string; readonly tools: InvestigationTools; readonly qualificationRef: string; } // Trusted daemon/provider injection only. qualificationRef identifies verified effective isolation, not a reviewer capability claim.

dataModelChanges.details: Exact sc7 ReviewClientStatusV1 is read from verified replay in proposed src/daemon/review-investigation-service.ts. covered counts required ledger rows with satisfied/finding/not-applicable dispositions; required is basis row count; pending/unverified and outstanding references remain unresolved. coverageRef is a private immutable snapshot reference authorized via daemon reads, never an artifact JSON ledger dump. generation and resume availability come from sc4 compatibility/lease/policy and current source; completed receipt is sc5-verified, transport failure is error with no verdict. Additional versioned envelope diagnostics expose latest durable block receipt/checkpoint/outstanding block IDs, provider liveness timestamp separately, usage pending/estimated/unavailable counts and allowance limits/preflight estimate with uncertainty. consumption.activeMs/continuationCount are sc4 accounting; estimatedInputTokens is an admission estimate, not observed spend. reportedRef refers only to deduplicated known observed usage; unknown counters stay null, pending outbox remains pending and cumulative snapshots are not added as model calls. Integrate the existing usage writer only when it guarantees idempotency; otherwise retain sc4 outbox, no new warehouse. MCP/daemon projections share one serializer and bounded heartbeat/status reads, not LLM summaries. Legacy diagnostics use engine:legacy, generation:0, resume unavailable, real observed phases and legacy dimension counts with explicit coverageUnit:legacy-dimension in the outer envelope; diagnostic subject digest binds existing BUILD fingerprint, not sc1 scope authority. Legacy missing identity returns explicit status-unavailable; no fabricated RecoveryStore or resumability.

Proposed codeReview.engine selection defaults to legacy; explicit plan-investigation-v1 starts require daemon/client schema support, reader support for investigation CR v1, qualified backend, approved predecessor code-only supersession record, and passing deterministic evaluation manifest tied to source commit/adapter/policy/fixture versions. A config switch alone cannot bypass readiness. Existing in-flight engine/transport identity is immutable across config changes. Before opt-in, use supported tracked amendment/tracking flow for predecessor S002/S003 code chunk/gather and S005 new CODE-review frames; do not edit approved sibling LLDs or design-review frames. Treat predecessor S005 installed and absent as separate tested partitions, preserve both installation orders and pre-S005 saved-state refusal/continuation semantics. Rollback disables new starts, revokes scheduling of new turns, pauses/drains existing attempts safely, keeps status/export/cancel and compatible frozen publication reconciliation; no silent conversion or loss of usage/receipts. A binary lacking investigation support refuses its resume IDs explicitly. Default replacement and live LLM comparison require separate explicit authorization and measured evidence; deterministic fixtures do not establish real defect recall or actual cloud token savings.

errorCases.scenario: Mixed or ambiguous commits, missing approved upstream, or changed canonical pins
errorCases.detection: sc1 canonical input verification and parent-relative attestation checks fail; freshness comparison observes different source/BUILD/contract revision/digest.
errorCases.response: Refuse before attempt issuance; return typed scope/stale reason with needed immutable selection. Never derive HEAD/working-tree fallback.
errorCases.userImpact: User corrects the approved scope or restarts with current contracts; no CR or model charge is manufactured.

errorCases.scenario: Unqualified native bridge or client/daemon schema mismatch
errorCases.detection: Capability handshake and effective tool/config catalogue do not match adapter/profile digest; engine/version discriminator or strict reply schema fails.
errorCases.response: unsupported-backend/unsupported-version with no provider call; never downgrade an explicit investigation request to broad legacy execution.
errorCases.userImpact: Legacy can be chosen explicitly for a separate new run; installation qualification or compatible client is needed for investigation.

errorCases.scenario: Wrong reviewer, forged capability, cross-run reply or expired generation
errorCases.detection: Canonical author versus authenticated reviewer comparison, capability MAC/epoch/expiry and sc3 run/subject/request/attempt/generation validation fail.
errorCases.response: Reject without invoking evidence or acceptance mutation. Revoke cancelled/old invocation capabilities and preserve accepted prefix.
errorCases.userImpact: Must use the independent reviewer party and current binding; late responses cannot corrupt another review.

errorCases.scenario: Caller discovery stale, unsupported language, missing changed entity or partial/empty index result
errorCases.detection: Graph source identity/registry closure/entity-to-packet mapping cannot be verified, or graph reports limited/unknown coverage.
errorCases.response: Keep explicit required impact obligation and limitations; require pinned caller inspection/accountable finding or unresolved outcome. Do not interpret empty results as no impact or silently switch modes.
errorCases.userImpact: Review can pause pending evidence; source-only remains an explicit separate mode with the same original scope/criteria.

errorCases.scenario: Transport detaches, provider times out, cancellation or daemon restarts
errorCases.detection: Connection loss is observed independently from owner lease and provider invocation; sc4 replay exposes issued/uncertain attempt and compatibility.
errorCases.response: Detach alone returns no verdict; retain bounded attempt and per-block ACKs. Timeout/abort drains callback authority and preserves unknown usage; restart claims new generation only through sc4. Same-run resume skips accepted work and never restarts a legacy volatile state.
errorCases.userImpact: Status explains actual durable progress and resume reason, not silence as failure/pass; only unfinished work continues.

errorCases.scenario: Same start identity reused with different inputs or concurrent resume
errorCases.detection: Immutable descriptor comparison differs, or sc4 current owner/generation refuses lease claim.
errorCases.response: Typed identity/ownership conflict; same exact start retries return original run. No duplicate attempts, separate acceptance log or new subject.
errorCases.userImpact: Caller reattaches or chooses a genuinely new requestId, without duplicated review spend.

errorCases.scenario: Canonical CR changed, publication ACK lost or callback deadline expires
errorCases.detection: sc5 frozen intent expected revision/head digest and canonical history verification detect conflict/uncertainty.
errorCases.response: Use sc5 reconciliation and frozen intent; no terminal receipt until verified canonical operation. Never rerun judges just for lost publication ACK; rendering retries only regenerate the view.
errorCases.userImpact: Stable completed result or explicit conflict/uncertainty; no spurious pass or automatic approval.

errorCases.scenario: Usage writer unavailable or legacy diagnostic state lost
errorCases.detection: Idempotent writer qualification fails/returns error, or volatile legacy state cannot be found after process restart.
errorCases.response: Keep sc4 pending usage with null unknown counters. Return explicit legacy status-unavailable/non-resumable; do not fabricate an investigation recovery record.
errorCases.userImpact: Consumption uncertainty stays visible; existing canonical CR still readable when present.

errorCases.scenario: Rollout evidence missing, predecessor schema overwrites successor route, or rollback binary cannot understand run
errorCases.detection: Adoption manifest hash, predecessor reconciliation approval, schema capability/partition tests or descriptor engine/version check is absent/mismatched.
errorCases.response: Keep opt-in closed; unknown resumes refuse. Rollback pauses/drains new turns but leaves compatible status/export/cancel and frozen publication reconciliation available.
errorCases.userImpact: Existing design and legacy review behavior remains isolated; enabling requires explicit validated migration evidence.

edgeCases.input: A tiny or planless BUILD with approved upstream and unplanned changed blocks
edgeCases.expected: Use sc1 approved-upstream route; criteria and every selected block remain required. Do not synthesize empty PLAN or omit unplanned scope.

edgeCases.input: Several reviewed blocks arrive within one managed native/controller session
edgeCases.expected: Each progress call obtains its own durable sc4 ACK before cursor advancement; final reply references them and has no new final coverage delta.

edgeCases.input: Same invocation final reply or progress ACK is retried after response loss
edgeCases.expected: Exact identity reuses accepted state/receipt; changed content under the same identity refuses.

edgeCases.input: Budgets exhausted while paused or waiting to execute
edgeCases.expected: Queue/idle/paused wall time is not consumed active time; no lease is held solely while waiting in the native execution queue. sc4 allowances require explicit extension and never reset on reconnect.

edgeCases.input: Legacy S005 installed before or after successor
edgeCases.expected: Both routing partitions preserve design-template/premise and valid legacy frames; only new explicit code-review engine routes to investigation. Older unsupported state versions refuse clearly.

edgeCases.input: Legacy status lacks detailed coverage or token observations
edgeCases.expected: Use explicitly labelled legacy-dimension diagnostics and null unavailable estimates, with resume unavailable; no synthetic evidence rows or exact autonomous call prediction.

migration.stateBefore: Discovery c1: completed S1-S5 provide internal domain/recovery/publication contracts with no production selection. Discovery c2: current provider runReviewSession has broad read tools/final answer only and no qualified scoped progress bridge. Discovery c3: codeReview.run/MCP step and predecessor S005 frames/design paths exist; no investigation engine flag is established.
migration.stateAfter: One daemon composition service and exact sc7 status serve explicit versioned investigation starts and recovery through qualified native/controller bridges. Legacy and design paths remain separate. Engine selection stays legacy by default; ready explicit opt-in is possible only after tracked predecessor reconciliation, compatible readers, qualified adapter and deterministic evidence. Real default adoption awaits separately authorized live comparison and user decision.

migrationSteps.action: Add additive shared types, daemon composition adapters, immutable descriptor discovery binding and scoped capability bridge with new starts disabled. Extend LLMProvider/CliProvider with the optional qualified investigation binding; absent binding keeps current behavior. Validate production descriptors and effective tool isolation before any model request.

Register version-discriminated new-engine IPC/MCP operations behind capability negotiation, keeping all valid original legacy and design frames on original handlers. Run both S005 installation orders, pre-S005 compatibility and cross-engine rejection fixtures. Update insrc_schema/insrc_guide and diagnostics from one authoritative registry.

Create the supported tracked predecessor amendment/reconciliation record superseding only S002/S003 code chunk/gather and S005 new CODE-review frames at adoption. Present it for explicit review/approval; do not silently rewrite approved sibling artifacts or touch design-review ownership. Bind readiness to its approved identity/revision.

Run deterministic independent-oracle parity, crash/concurrency, native isolation, status/usage and baseline metric fixtures; record source/policy/schema/adapter/fixture hashes and evidence quality. Unknown/live-unmeasured values stay explicit. Install compatible daemon and client together through existing update procedure; restart creates no conversion of old volatile state.

Allow an explicitly chosen plan-investigation-v1 start only when all readiness predicates hold. Existing runs retain original engine/version. Do not flip the default or claim cloud token/defect-quality gains from deterministic tests; authorized live comparison and a later explicit adoption decision are required for any default change.

Rollback sets selection to legacy and rejects new investigation starts/turns while safely draining or pausing current attempts. Preserve compatible status/export/cancel, usage outbox and frozen completion reconciliation. Re-enabling requires the original pinned descriptor compatibility; unsupported older binaries explicitly refuse resume and retain runtime files for a compatible daemon.

migration.backwardCompat: Additive explicit engine/version discrimination; no existing caller is forced onto investigation. Legacy full/degraded CRs and v1 investigation records remain readable by compatible readers. Original legacy/controller states finish only through supported original handlers; lost volatile legacy states stay non-resumable. Design template and premise reviews are unchanged, and installation-order fixtures protect both owners. No ledger migration, native-session-to-domain conversion, automatic BUILD approval, tracker action or default change.

Version-discriminate legacy calls and plan-investigation-v1 commands; both transports invoke the same read/progress/reply authority.
